newsitem.title: USA: ABC/Money consumer comfort index -9 Nov 10 week.
newsitem.headline: ABC/Money consumer comfort index -9 Nov 10 week.

text.p: The Money Magazine/ABC News consumer comfort index remained unchanged at -9 in the week ended November 10.

The survey, this time with 1,032 respondents, polls consumers nationwide about the national economy, their own finances and their willingness to spend money. The poll has a margin of error of plus/minus 3.5 percent.
Respondents' confidence in the economy rose to -14 from -16 the previous week.
Confidence in personal finances fell to 14 from 16, and Americans' rating of buying climate fell two points to -28.
Regionally, confidence fell in the South and West, while it rose in the Northeast and Midwest, according to the index.
During the two weeks ending November 10, Money Magazine/ABC News also polled 519 adults -- directly before and after the election -- on what should be "the next President's top financial priority."

Twenty-nine percent of the respondents said cutting taxes should take top financial priorty. But a statistically equal portion of 24 percent said the President should focus first on lowering the budget deficit, while another 22 percent said his chief financial goal should keep the unemployment rate low.
Some 15 percent said keeping inflation low should top the list, while six percent favored lowering interest rates, according to the poll.
